sources.locator: Complete 150-page faculty-hosted PDF. contents.name: Section 5.2: finite-history normal equations, mean adjustment and error-variance identity
Section 5.2: uniqueness of the forecast class, posed in the notes as a homework exercise
contents.reason: The homework gap is completed locally by the published affine L2 projection theorem; only uniqueness of the predictor class is claimed for singular history covariance.

contents.name: Section 5.2: joint Gaussianity makes the finite-history affine projection the conditional mean
contents.reason: The notes state the result but do not give the required residual-independence proof; the local theorem proves it using the Gaussian block-independence lemma.

contents.name: Section 5.5.1: Durbin–Levinson coefficient and variance recurrences with a projection-based proof
contents.reason: The source assumes gamma(h) tends to zero to obtain strict positive definiteness. The local algorithm instead states positive definiteness of the required leading blocks and the local induction verifies the recurrences under exactly that condition.

contents.name: Proposition 5.1: gamma(h) tending to zero implies positive-definite history matrices
contents.reason: The planned result assumes positive-definite leading blocks directly and does not claim this additional covariance-decay implication.

sources.title: Probability: Theory and Examples, 5th ed.
sources.locator: Complete 490-page fifth-edition PDF. Inspected Section 3.10, printed pp. 202–203 (PDF markers 208–210): construction of multivariate-normal laws from a positive-semidefinite covariance, including degenerate cases, and Exercise 3.10.7, which states the zero-off-diagonal covariance independence criterion for coordinates.

contents.name: Section 3.10 Gaussian law construction including degenerate covariance; Exercise 3.10.7 states the coordinate independence criterion
contents.reason: Exercise 3.10.7 states the coordinate criterion but leaves its proof as an exercise and does not directly cover within-block dependence; the assigned block result is proved locally by the block square-root and characteristic-function argument.

sources.title: J. R. Norris, Probability and Measure, complete lecture notes
sources.locator: Complete 54-page PDF; Sections 8.1–8.2 were read in full, printed pp. 36–37 (PDF markers 36–37), especially Theorem 8.2.1(b),(c),(e) and its complete proof: affine images remain Gaussian, the characteristic function is determined by mean and covariance, and zero cross-covariance between Gaussian vector blocks gives independence without an invertibility assumption.

contents.name: Section 8.2, Theorem 8.2.1(e): Gaussian blocks with zero cross-covariance are independent
